newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand's Vortec plans NZSE listing.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand's Vortec plans NZSE listing.

text.p: Vortec Energy Ltd said on Monday it planned a public share offer in May, which was expected to be the last issue of shares before the company sought a listing on the New Zealand Stock Exchange.
Vortec, formerly Advanced Windpower, has designed a wind turbine which it says is capable of producing electricity six to eight times more efficiently than conventional turbines.
A scaled down prototype is being assembled on a west coast site about 100 kilometres south of Auckland.

The Vortec is a wind turbine with the assistance of an a aerodynamic device called a diffuser, which creates a low pressure region downstream of the turbine rotor. This leads to a suction effect, doubling the ambient windspeed at the rotor.
The one-third size prototype is about seven storeys tall.

"If Vortec 7 performs to expectation, windpower is set to become the environmentally friendly energy source that is at last competitive with all other forms of power generation," Managing Director Robin Johannink said in a statement.
At the demonstrator site at Waikaretu, Counties Power have supplied high voltage cables to connect Vortec 7 to the grid.
The performance of the turbine will be evaluated by Industrial Research Ltd and Auckland University, assisted by a NZ$500,000 grant from the Ministry of Science.
Vortec Energy, which has 100 shareholders at present, has the world rights to produce the turbine.
The company was formed two years ago after reaching a 20-year agreement with Northrop Grumman.
Northrop developed the initial diffuser design, put it through wind tunnel testing, but did not take the project through to construction.
No other details on Vortec's listing plans were immediately available.
